title: IPSec tunnels to ZIA: limits, IKE and device settings

prose.text: IPSec is the tunnel for routers that cannot do GRE and for sites with changing addresses. {{when-ipsec}} The credential that identifies the site is its own object: [[zia.traffic-forwarding.vpn-credentials]].

Whether the local ID matches the credential type.

when-ipsec.statement: IPSec tunnels are the option when the router does not support GRE or the site has dynamic IP addresses. Compared with GRE it adds processing overhead on the customer's equipment, and the vendor must provide a VPN failover mechanism.

quotes: If your router does not support GRE or if you use dynamic IP addresses, you can configure IPSec VPN tunnels.
Compared to GRE tunnels, IPSec tunnels have additional processing overhead on your equipment.
Ensure that your vendor provides a VPN fail over mechanism to provide resilience.

two-tunnels.statement: Zscaler recommends two IPSec tunnels to two different Public Service Edges, a primary and a backup; if the primary or an intermediate connection fails, traffic is rerouted through the backup tunnel.

quotes: Zscaler recommends configuring two separate VPNs to two different Public Service Edges for high availability.
If the primary IPSec VPN tunnel or if an intermediate connection goes down, all traffic is then rerouted through the backup IPSec VPN tunnel to the backup Public Service Edge.

bandwidth-limit.statement: IPSec tunnels support 400 Mbps per public source IP address. Above that, use multiple tunnels with different public source IPs, or multiple tunnels from the same public source IP with NAT-T and source port randomization using IKEv2; 800 Mbps is two primary and two backup tunnels.

quotes: Zscaler IPSec tunnels support a limit of 400 Mbps for each public source IP address.
Configure multiple IPSec VPN tunnels with the same public source IP address using NAT-T and source port randomization with IKEv2 for all the configured tunnels.
if your organization forwards 800 Mbps of traffic, you can configure two primary VPN tunnels and two backup VPN tunnels
Configure multiple IPSec tunnels with different public source IP addresses.

ike-versions.statement: Zscaler recommends IKEv2. New tenants cannot establish IKEv1 IPSec tunnels from a vendor product to forward traffic to Internet & SaaS unless Zscaler Support enables IKEv1 for them.

quotes: Zscaler recommends using IKEv2 because it is a newer standard and is widely deployed.
New tenants cannot establish IKEv1 IPSec VPN tunnels from a vendor product to forward traffic to Internet & SaaS. To enable IKEv1 support for new tenants, contact Zscaler Support.

ikev1-modes.statement: With IKEv1 and a pre-shared key, a peer identified by FQDN must use Aggressive mode and a peer identified by a static IP must use Main mode; Main mode cannot be used where the peer's IP may change.

quotes: If you use a pre-shared key (PSK) for authentication and an FQDN for the peer, you must use Aggressive mode. If you use a PSK for authentication and a static IP address for the peer, you must use the Main mode.
Because the Main mode uses the IP address as part of the exchange for identification, it cannot be used in a configuration where the IP address of the peer may change.

ikev2-parameters.statement: For IKEv2 the supported Phase 1 values are AES-256/192/128 or 3DES, SHA-512/384/256/1, Diffie-Hellman groups 2, 5, 14, 19, 20 and 21, with a pre-shared key and 24-hour SA lifetime; Phase 2 supports ESP or AH in tunnel mode with AES-GCM, NULL or AES, 8 child SAs and an 8-hour lifetime. The table lists NAT-T and DPD as options (DPD timeout 20 seconds, 5 retries).

| Integrity | SHA-512 SHA-384 SHA-256 SHA-1 | MD5 SHA-512 SHA-384 SHA-256 SHA-1 |

ikev2-parameters.conditions: The table lists values Zscaler supports; which of them a tenant's device negotiates is not visible from these sources.

mtu-mss.statement: The vendor's IPSec table gives an optimal MTU of 1400 bytes and an MSS of 1360 bytes for Phase 2, for both IKEv2 and IKEv1.

quotes: | Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) | N/A | Your Optimal MTU 1400 Bytes |
| Maximum Segment Size (MSS) | N/A | 1360 Bytes |

header-length.statement: In the MTU calculation for GRE or IPSec tunnels, the IPSec tunnel header length is variable and can be up to 64 bytes; if the organization experiences issues performing the page's tasks, Zscaler recommends a tunnel MTU of 1400.

quotes: For IPSec tunnel, the header length is variable and can be up to 64 bytes.
If you experience issues performing the tasks above, Zscaler recommends that you use a tunnel MTU of 1400.

nat-traversal.statement: Zscaler supports NAT-Traversal when the initiating device is behind a NAT device; the packets are then encapsulated in UDP with source port 4500. NAT-T is built into IKEv2 and an optional extension to IKEv1.

quotes: Zscaler supports NAT-Traversal if the device initiating the IPSec VPN is behind another firewall or router performing NAT.
In the UDP header, the source port is set to 4500 and the destination port is that of the IPSec peer.
NAT-T is integrated into IKEv2 but is an optional extension to IKEv1.

dpd.statement: Zscaler expects peers to run explicit periodic liveness checks (DPD) where the devices support them, and recommends 10 to 20 second intervals with at least 3 retries; if only on-demand checks are supported the Zscaler IP must be allowlisted so Zscaler's DPD gets a response, and with no response Zscaler cleans up the connection. Ongoing traffic is not treated as proof the peer is alive.

quotes: Zscaler expects the peers to do explicit periodic liveliness checks to confirm that the DPD flow is continuous, if it is supported on the devices.
Zscaler recommends a minimum of 10-second to a maximum of 20-second DPD intervals with at least 3 retries.

If the periodic liveliness check is not supported (i.e., only on-demand check is supported), you must ensure to allowlist the Zscaler IP address so that DPD initiated by Zscaler is not blocked, and a response is received.
If there is no response, Zscaler cleans up the connection.
Zscaler does not consider the ongoing flow of traffic between two peers as proof of the liveliness of a peer.

local-id.statement: The device's local ID can be a private IP address only when the VPN credential in the Admin Console is an FQDN; otherwise it should be the public IP provisioned as a static IP. A private local ID with a public IP credential makes the negotiation fail.

quotes: the local ID of the peer device on the client side can be a private IP address if the VPN credential configured in the Zscaler Admin Console is a fully qualified domain name (FQDN).
If the local ID is a private IP address and a public IP address is configured in the Zscaler Admin Console, then the negotiation fails.
Otherwise, the local ID should be a public IP address. The public IP address is provisioned as a static IP address, which is then used to add a VPN credential to the Zscaler Admin Console.

ipv6-selectors.statement: To forward IPv6 over IPSec the device needs IPv6 traffic selectors for both IKEv1 and IKEv2, and IPv6 support must be enabled for the organization and its locations.

quotes: If you want to forward IPv6 traffic to Internet & SaaS (ZIA), you must configure IPv6 traffic selectors for both IKEv1 and IKEv2 on your device.
You must also ensure that IPv6 support is enabled for your organization and locations in the Zscaler Admin Console to forward IPv6 traffic.

device-guides-rfc1918.statement: Each of the seven IPSec device guides (Cisco ASA 55xx, Cisco 881 ISR, Juniper SRX, Juniper SSG 20, FortiGate, Palo Alto Networks, SonicWall TZ 350) says tunnel interface configuration must use RFC 1918 addresses, not APIPA addresses.

quotes: For tunnel interface configuration, you must use only RFC 1918 IP addresses and not APIPA addresses.

no-esn.statement: All seven device guides say Zscaler does not support Extended Sequence Number (ESN) based proposals in IPSec tunnel negotiation; one section of the Cisco ASA guide says "configuration" where another says "negotiations".

quotes: Zscaler does not support Extended Sequence Number (ESN) based proposals during IPSec tunnel negotiations.

phase2-sa-count.statement: The Cisco ASA guide says Zscaler supports up to 8 Phase 2 SAs: one is used for the connection between the ASA's public IP address and the Public Service Edges, leaving seven for subnets that flow through the tunnel.

quotes: Zscaler supports up to 8 Phase 2 SAs, as shown in the preceding example for version 9.6. One SA is used for the connection between the Cisco ASA’s public IP address and the Public Service Edges. You can then configure seven subnets to flow through the tunnel, forming the remaining seven SAs.

main-mode-source-ip.statement: The Cisco ASA guide says the public source IP address is required only to set up an IPSec tunnel in Phase 1 main mode.

quotes: The public source IP address is only required if you want to set up an IPSec tunnel in phase one main mode.

asa-specifics.statement: In the Cisco ASA guide's section for version 9.6, the policy numbered #1 must be the Zscaler policy or the tunnel negotiations fail; the ASA's default Phase 2 SA lifetime of 8 hours (28800 seconds) equals Zscaler's recommended value; and traffic through the tunnel must keep its source IP address.

quotes: This policy is defined as #1, which can conflict with an existing policy. If so, Zscaler recommends changing your existing policy number because the #1 policy must be the Zscaler policy. Otherwise, the tunnel negotiations fail.
You don't need to change the default SA lifetime value, which is 8 hours (28800 seconds), because it is the same as the Zscaler recommended value for Phase 2.
Traffic that flows through the tunnel must maintain its source IP address.

one-tunnel-active.statement: The Cisco 881 ISR guide says both tunnels are configured at the gateway but only one is operational at a time; the second is a backup.

quotes: Both tunnels must be configured at your gateway. Only a single tunnel is operational at any time. The second tunnel acts as a backup tunnel.

no-lifesize.statement: The Palo Alto Networks guide says to keep the Enable option unchecked because Zscaler does not support life size; the Juniper SSG 20 guide enters 0 bytes for the Phase 2 lifetime in Kbytes.

quotes: Keep the Enable option unchecked because Zscaler does not support life size.
In Kbytes: Enter 0 bytes.

ping-both-edges.statement: The Cisco 881 ISR and Palo Alto Networks guides say to contact Zscaler Support if the admin is unable to ping both Public Service Edge IP addresses.

quotes: If you are unable to ping both Public Service Edge IP addresses, contact Zscaler Support.
If you are unable to ping both Public Service Edge IP addresses, contact Zscaler Support.

pan-monitoring.statement: The Palo Alto Networks guide says the Public Service Edge VIP locations must correspond to the Public Service Edge IP locations, that PAN-OS uses ICMP probes for tunnel and policy-based forward monitoring, and that the destination IP is the Virtual IP address of the primary tunnel (165.225.80.34 in the example).

quotes: Ensure that the locations of the Public Service Edge Virtual IP addresses correspond to the locations of the Public Service Edge IP addresses.
Palo Alto Networks uses ICMP probes for tunnel and policy-based forward monitoring.
Destination IP: Enter the Virtual IP address of your primary tunnel. In this example, it's 165.225.80.34.

pac-and-ip-sla.statement: The Cisco 881 ISR guide says that when PAC files forward traffic through the tunnel, IP SLA monitoring and the PAC files must use different Global Public Service Edge IP addresses; with the same ones, the PAC files send all packets through the same tunnel whatever the tunnel interface state.

quotes: If you use PAC files to forward traffic through the tunnel, ensure that you use different Global Public Service Edge IP addresses for IP SLA monitoring and your PAC files.
Using the same Global Public Service Edge IP addresses causes the PAC files to send all packets through the same tunnel regardless of the tunnel interface state.

ikev2-device-versions.statement: IKEv2 needs Cisco IOS 15.1.1T or later on a Cisco 881 ISR, and version 19.2R2.7 or later on a Juniper SRX 300.

quotes: You must have a Cisco 881 ISR running Cisco IOS version 15.1.1T or later to configure IKEv2.
You must have a Juniper SRX 300 router running version 19.2R2.7 or later to configure IKEv2.

device-failover.statement: The Juniper SRX guide requires both DPD and VPN monitoring for failover; the Juniper SSG 20 and SonicWall TZ 350 guides require DPD, and the SonicWall TZ 350 does not support VPN monitoring and relies on DPD for failover.

quotes: Dead Peer Detection (DPD) and VPN monitoring must be enabled so the firewall can detect if one VPN goes offline and moves the internet-bound traffic to the other VPN.
Dead Peer Detection (DPD) must be enabled, so the firewall can detect if a VPN is offline.
Dead Peer Detection (DPD) must be enabled, so the firewall can detect if a VPN is offline.
SonicWall TZ 350 firewall doesn't support VPN monitoring. It relies on DPD for failover.

fortinet-np-offload.statement: The FortiGate guide says the network processor of some Fortinet devices does not support offloading VPN phase one traffic, which causes an unacceptable drop in tunnel performance.

quotes: The network processor (NP) of some Fortinet devices doesn’t support offloading VPN phase one traffic, resulting in an unacceptable drop in VPN tunnel performance.

srx-ecmp.statement: The Juniper SRX guide says ECMP flow-based forwarding can optionally be configured to load-balance the tunnels if multiple virtual IP addresses are configured in the Zscaler data center for the VPN tunnels.

quotes: You can optionally configure ECMP flow-based forwarding on your Juniper SRX router to enable load balancing for your tunnels if multiple virtual IP addresses are configured in your Zscaler data center for the VPN tunnels.

srx-ecmp.conditions: How to obtain multiple virtual IP addresses in a Zscaler data center is not stated.

finding-vpn-hosts.statement: Under VPN Host Name, the admin finds the two data centers closest to the organization's location and chooses one as the destination of the primary tunnel and the other as that of the backup, and the hostnames of those destinations are resolved when IP addresses are needed. The cloud name is in the URL admins use to log in.

quotes: Under VPN Host Name, find the two data centers closest to the organization's location. Choose one as the destination for your primary IPSec VPN tunnel and the other as the destination for your backup IPSec VPN tunnel.
If you need the IP addresses of the Public Service Edges, resolve the hostnames of your primary and backup destinations.
You can find the name of your cloud in the URL your admins used to log in to the Zscaler service.

dpd-device-guides.summary: Zscaler recommends DPD intervals of 10 to 20 seconds with at least 3 retries, but the device guides use values inside, below and above that range, and one uses on-demand DPD.

quotes: Zscaler recommends a minimum of 10-second to a maximum of 20-second DPD intervals with at least 3 retries.

If the periodic liveliness check is not supported (i.e., only on-demand check is supported), you must ensure to allowlist the Zscaler IP address so that DPD initiated by Zscaler is not blocked, and a response is received.

positions.says: DPD intervals of 10 to 20 seconds with at least 3 retries; on-demand-only devices must allowlist the Zscaler IP address.

quotes: crypto ikev2 dpd 10 5 periodic

positions.says: The Cisco 881 ISR guide configures `crypto ikev2 dpd 10 5 periodic`: periodic DPD with an interval of 10 (inside the recommended range).

quotes: set security ike gateway <Primary IKE Gateway Name> dead-peer-detection interval 20
set security ike gateway <Primary IKE Gateway Name> dead-peer-detection threshold 5

positions.says: The Juniper SRX guide sets interval 20 and threshold 5 (inside the recommended range).

quotes: Select DPD under Peer Status Detection.
Interval: Enter 5 seconds.
Retry: Enter 5 seconds.

positions.says: The Juniper SSG 20 guide enables DPD with an interval of 5 seconds (below 10).

quotes: Liveness Check: Select this checkbox.
Interval: Enter 5.

positions.says: The Palo Alto Networks guide enables the liveness check with an interval of 5 (below 10).

quotes: Dead Peer Detection Interval (seconds): Enter 60.
Failure Trigger Level (missed heartbeats): Enter 3.

positions.says: The SonicWall TZ 350 guide sets a DPD interval of 60 seconds with a failure trigger level of 3 (above 20).

quotes: Dead Peer Detection: Select On Demand.

positions.says: The FortiGate guide selects On Demand DPD.

dpd-device-guides.impact: Copying a device guide can leave a device outside Zscaler's stated DPD expectation; under dpd, Zscaler cleans up a connection that gets no DPD response.

srx-sa-lifetimes.summary: The Juniper SRX guide sets IKE and IPSec proposal lifetimes of 3600 seconds, while the IKEv2 table lists SA lifetimes of 24 hours for Phase 1 and 8 hours for Phase 2, and the Cisco ASA guide says its 8-hour default equals Zscaler's recommended Phase 2 value.

quotes: set security ike proposal <IKE Proposal Name> lifetime-seconds 3600
set security ipsec proposal <IPSec Proposal Name> lifetime-seconds 3600

positions.says: The Juniper SRX example sets both proposal lifetimes to 3600 seconds.

quotes: | SA Lifetime | 24 Hours | 8 Hours |

positions.says: The IKEv2 table lists an SA lifetime of 24 hours for Phase 1 and 8 hours for Phase 2.

quotes: You don't need to change the default SA lifetime value, which is 8 hours (28800 seconds), because it is the same as the Zscaler recommended value for Phase 2.

positions.says: The Cisco ASA guide leaves its 8-hour default because it matches Zscaler's recommended Phase 2 value.

srx-sa-lifetimes.impact: Low: the table may give Zscaler's own lifetimes, which a shorter peer value negotiates under, but no page says whether 3600 seconds is acceptable.

ipsec-protocol.summary: The NSS tunnel output format says Zscaler only supports ESP for the IPSec tunnel protocol, while the IKEv2 supported parameters table lists AH and ESP.

quotes: | %s{tunnelprotocol} | The IPSec tunnel protocol type. Zscaler only supports ESP. | None ISAKMP AH ESP IPCOMP | IPSec Protocol |
| Protocol | N/A | AH ESP |

positions.says: The IKEv2 table lists the protocol as AH ESP.

ipsec-protocol.impact: Whether an AH tunnel is supported depends on which page is read; the pages do not say whether the table row lists supported or merely defined values.

esp-overhead-range.title: ESP overhead and effective MTU range
esp-overhead-range.detail: Unverified legacy statement: IPSec ESP adds about 50 to 80 bytes of overhead, giving an effective payload MTU of about 1380 to 1420 bytes depending on cipher and NAT-T. No captured source states it; the MTU article says only that the IPSec tunnel header length is variable and can be up to 64 bytes (header-length). Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.

failing-mss-symptom.title: Large-transfer failures without MSS clamping on IPSec
failing-mss-symptom.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Failing to set MSS under IPSec more commonly causes large-transfer failures than under GRE because the overhead is higher. No captured source states it; operator experience or a tenant observation would settle it.
